title: A billing protection can change provider participation without proving lower patient costs
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office claims analysis of provider participation and payments before and after the No Surprises Act
geography: United States privately insured health-care claims; selected specialties, 2019-2023

observations.period: 2019-2023; four specialties most likely to be affected by No Surprises protections

denominator.unit: emergency medicine, radiology, anesthesiology, and air ambulance specialties

in_network_claims.value: the percentage of in-network claims increased after the Act took effect for three of four specialties

emergency_medicine_pattern.value: facility and professional in-network claim shares declined before implementation and increased afterward

interpretation.value: higher in-network claim shares may indicate increased provider participation

observations.method: GAO analysis of a large private health-insurance claims dataset and interviews with 20 stakeholder groups, including providers, issuers, and state insurance departments.
observations.uncertainty: In-network claim share is an indicator rather than a direct measure of contracting, patient experience, or the law's isolated causal effect.
observations.subgroup: Privately insured claims in four selected specialties likely to be affected by the balance-billing prohibition.
observations.counterinterpretation: The post-law shift may reflect other market changes, and higher in-network claims do not automatically mean lower patient bills or better care.

denominator.unit: inflation-adjusted payment trends for selected emergency-medicine services

facility_payment.value: in-network emergency facility payments increased in 2022 and 2023

professional_payment.value: in-network emergency physician or practice payments decreased in 2022 and 2023

pre_law_continuity.value: payment changes largely continued trends that began before the Act

observations.method: GAO analysis of inflation-adjusted claim payments before and after January 1, 2022 implementation.
observations.uncertainty: Payment trends do not identify patient liability, provider costs, insurer margins, or the causal effect of the Act.
observations.subgroup: Selected emergency-medicine facility and professional claims.
observations.counterinterpretation: The law may still have affected negotiations or billing protection even where payment trends followed earlier paths.

boundary: This record measures selected provider claim-network shares and payment trends before and after the No Surprises Act. It does not establish patient bills, out-of-pocket cost, care access, health outcomes, or an isolated causal effect.
